notes: PLACEHOLDER DATA — these are NOT real interview quotes. They were hand-authored to populate the demo UI alongside the synthetic LN cluster usage (lupus_nephritis_keyword_usage.json) and the manual-estimate search files under disease-insights/lupus-nephritis/search/.

One quote per canonical topic category in topic-alignment.ts. Attribution uses the same ln_01..ln_04 synthetic participant ids that lupus_nephritis_keyword_usage.json uses, so participant counts and quote counts stay internally consistent.

Replace this file with real transcript-anchored quotes once a real LN corpus exists; the consuming code (narrativeForTopicRow in topic-alignment.ts) looks each quote up by category_id, so a real-data replacement only needs to preserve the key shape.

quotes.text: It's a different kind of tired. After sleeping ten hours, your bones are still tired. People don't get that until they see it.
They told me my eGFR was forty-three and I was supposed to know what that meant. I went home and Googled it for an hour before I understood I had stage three kidney disease.
My doctor switched me to Lupkynis after the mycophenolate stopped working. I had to ask her how to pronounce it. None of these drug names sound like real words.
The prednisone gave me the moon face within six weeks. I stopped sending photos to family — I told my husband I felt like I was wearing a costume of someone else's body.
I had to leave my teaching job. I couldn't be in a room with thirty unvaccinated kids while I was immunocompromised. That decision broke something in me.
My grandmother went on dialysis at the end. When my nephrologist said a transplant might be on the table in five years, I just — I had to leave the office.
I read about a CAR-T trial that sounded promising — it's in Boston and I'm in Albuquerque. I never even brought it up with my doctor.
